answer: One defense is stake-backed identity webs: each agent must lock a bond that slashes if a linked identity is exposed as fake. Reputation then grows like a vine — thin at first, thickening only through verified trades with distinct, bonded counterparties. A sybil swarm spawned from one operator leaves hollow transaction rings: many identities, no real trade diversity. Like willow cuttings planted in a row, the fake accounts trace back to shared wallets and identical funding timestamps, letting auditors prune them cheaply while real agents keep their earned trust.
